header: Order or other proceedings with signature of Judge(s).
Present:- Mr. Noor Zada Khan Ahmadzai,
body: MUHAMMAD TARIQ AFRIDI, J.- Appellant, Shahi Marjan, has preferred the instant criminal appeal under Section 417(2-A) Cr.P.C. against the judgment, dated 23.12.2021, passed by the learned Sessions Judge/Judge Special Court, North Waziristan at Bannu, whereby accused/respondent Noor Ayaz was acquitted in case FIR No.44, dated 02.12.2019, registered under Section 15 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Arms Act, 2013, at Police Station Mir Ali, District North Waziristan.
2. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and gone through the record.

3. At the very outset, the maintainability of the instant appeal is to be examined. The appellant, being a private person, has called in question the acquittal of the accused/respondent in an offence arising under the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Arms Act, 2013. Section 417(2- A), Cr.P.C. confers a statutory right upon a “complainant” to file an appeal against acquittal. However, this right is available only in respect of cases instituted upon a private complaint under Chapter XVI of the Cr.P.C. and does not extend to State cases, particularly those arising under special enactments like the Arms Act, which are cognizable by the police and prosecuted by the State. In such like cases, the right to appeal against acquittal is exclusively vested in the Provincial Government under Section 417(1), Cr.P.C. Since the present FIR was registered by the police under Section 15 of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Arms Act, 2013, the case is a State case, and the complainant/ appellant has no locus standi to maintain an appeal against acquittal. The only competent authority in such matters is the Provincial Government, which may file appeal under Section 417(1), Cr.P.C.
4. In view of the above legal position, the instant appeal being incompetent is not maintainable and accordingly stands dismissed in limine.
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Tariq Afridi Hon'ble Mr. Justice Abdul Fayaz
